extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (applicants/attorneys)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for examination and prosecution of U.S. patent applications under the MPEP Chapter 700 series, covering statutory bases (35 U.S.C. 101/102/103/111/112), searching, rejections, interviews, amendments, affidavits, patentability reports, and related procedural matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory Authority for Examination (35 U.S.C. 131 / 35 U.S.C. 101)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner shall cause an examination to be made of the application and the alleged new invention; and if on such examination it appears that the applicant is entitled to a patent under the law, the Commissioner shall issue a patent therefor. The main conditions precedent to the grant of a patent are set forth in 35 U.S.C. 101, 102 and 103. 35 U.S.C. 101: Whoever invents or discovers any new and useful process, machine, manufacture, or composition of matter, or any new and useful improvement thereof, may obtain a patent therefor, subject to the conditions and requirements of this title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner must apply statutory standards (101/102/103) when deciding allowance. MPEP reproduces statutory definitions (35 U.S.C. 100) for terms like 'invention' and 'process'. Use Form Paragraph 7.04 for copying 35 U.S.C. 101. Ensure issues pertinent to patentability are raised and resolved during examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requisites of the Application (35 U.S.C. 111(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: When a new application is assigned in the examining group, the examiner should review contents to determine if the application meets the requirements of 35 U.S.C. 111(a). Matters affecting filing date or abandonment (lack of oath/declaration, filing fee, or claims) should be checked before placing the application in storage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners must ensure the application meets MPEP Chapter 600 requisites (formal matters and completeness/clarity of disclosure). If requisites are not met, applicant may be called for necessary amendments, which must not include new matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling Obviously Informal or Incomprehensible Cases
rubrics_metrics.description: If impractical to give a complete action on the merits because of an informal or insufficient disclosure, follow procedures: (A) make a reasonable search as far as disclosure can be understood; (B) point out informalities and drawing deficiencies via attachments; (C) require revision to idiomatic English and U.S. practice; (D) reject claims as failing to define the invention under 35 U.S.C. 112 if informal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If disclosure is incomprehensible, inform applicant that no search was made. Treat a number of obviously informal claims as a single claim for fee and examination purposes. Encourage preliminary amendment within ~3 months to correct informalities but prohibit new matter. Use the appropriate form paragraphs (7.01, 7.02, 7.03) and set shortened statutory period for reply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Terminology — Cannot Be Examined (Form Paragraphs 7.01–7.03)
rubrics_metrics.description: If terminology is so different from art-accepted terms that a proper prior art search cannot be made, require applicant to clarify or correlate terminology with art-accepted terminology or supply amended disclosure. If portions are illegible, require substitute specification or amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.01 when terminology prevents proper search; 7.02 when disclosure is incomprehensible; 7.03 for illegible pages. Indicate specific pages/items that are problematic. Warn applicant not to introduce new matter. Set shortened statutory period for reply (ONE MONTH or THIRTY DAYS, whichever is longer).

rubrics_metrics.name: Search: Understand Invention Before Searching
rubrics_metrics.description: After reading the specification and claims, the examiner searches the prior art. The invention should be thoroughly understood before a search is undertaken; nevertheless, informal or imperfectly understood cases are also given a search to avoid piecemeal prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP Chapter 900 for detailed search guidance. When assigned after another examiner, give full faith and credit to prior examiner's search and action unless there's clear error or knowledge of other prior art. Generally avoid entirely new approach or new search just to hope of finding something.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability Reports (P.R.) — When and How to Use
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an application contains claims classifiable in other groups and claims are not divisible inter se, the application may be referred to other group(s) for a Patentability Report. The P.R. includes citation of pertinent references and complete action on all involved claims; it is signed by the primary examiner in the reporting group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: P.R. practice is to be used only in extraordinary circumstances and primarily where it will save total examiner time or improve quality due to specialized knowledge. The forwarding group must approve and the Group Director of the requesting group must approve. The P.R. is returned to the original group and placed in the file wrapper; if the jurisdictional examiner agrees with the P.R., incorporate substance into action. P.R. is not a transfer; counting/recording rules apply; duplicate drawings may be furnished to reporting group for interference searches. Avoid P.R. where one examiner can complete examination in less total examiner time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence of Examination in P.R. Cases
rubrics_metrics.description: If supervisory patent examiners cannot agree as to order of examination by groups, the supervisory examiner having jurisdiction will direct a complete search be made prior to referring the application for report; reporting group will be advised of results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a different sequence of search is expedient, modify order accordingly. Where claims are directed to same character of invention but differ only in scope, P.R. is never proper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection of Claims — General Standard and Practice (37 CFR 1.104)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the invention is not considered patentable, or not patentable as claimed, the claims (or those considered unpatentable) will be rejected. In rejecting claims for want of novelty or for obviousness, the examiner must cite the best references and designate the particular part relied on when reference is complex. The pertinence of each reference must be clearly explained and each rejected claim specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The goal is to articulate any rejection early so applicant can reply and provide evidence. Examiner should review all evidence, arguments, and responsive evidence before issuing next Office action. Examiner may rely on admissions by applicant or facts within knowledge (including 102(f)/(g) prior art as permitted under 103). When multiple features present in reference, designate parts relied upon as nearly as practicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform Application of the Patentability Standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards of patentability must be the same throughout the Office. All requirements (novelty, usefulness, unobviousness — 35 U.S.C. 101/102/103) must be met before a claim is allowed. The standard to be applied is the 'preponderance of the evidence' test: reject a claim if, in view of prior art and evidence, it is more likely than not that the claim is unpatentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not allow applications unless and until issues pertinent to patentability have been raised and resolved in examination/prosecution. The mere level of detail in a claim ('picture' claim) is not justification for allowance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction Between Rejection and Objection
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'rejection' refuses to grant claims because subject matter is unpatentable (merits), while an 'objection' addresses improper claim form. Rejections are subject to Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences review; objections (formal matters) generally are reviewable only by petition to the Commissioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not combine formal objections with rejections in appeals improperly. Use the terms accurately in examiner's action. Examples: dependency on a rejected claim is a form matter and treated as an objection if dependent claim otherwise allowable.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 102 — Conditions for Patentability (Novelty / Loss of Right)
rubrics_metrics.description: A person shall be entitled to a patent unless: (a) invention was known/used by others in this country, or patented/described in a printed publication before the invention by the applicant; (b) invention was patented/described in a printed publication or in public use/on sale more than one year prior to U.S. filing; (c) abandonment; (d) prior foreign patent/application more than 12 months earlier; (e) earlier U.S. patent/application by another; (f) applicant did not himself invent; (g) priority/interference rules under subsection (g).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When applying 102 rejections, identify the statutory subsection relied upon. Use best references and explain pertinence. See MPEP subsections for printed publication/patent (706.02(b)), knowledge by others/public use/sale (706.02(c)), 102(e) provisional rejections, 102(f) and 102(g) procedures. For complicated references, designate the particular part relied upon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overcoming a 35 U.S.C. 102 Rejection Based on a Printed Publication or Patent
rubrics_metrics.description: When a rejection is based on a printed publication or patent, applicant may overcome by showing the reference is not enabling, is not a printed publication, shows different invention, or by establishing earlier effective filing date or other statutory exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide specifics: point to non-enablement, differences in structure/limitations, affidavits/declarations if appropriate, or antedating evidence. See MPEP §706.02(b) for form paragraphs and specific procedures (not exhaustively reproduced here).

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 103 — Nonobviousness Rejections (Contents and Practice)
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent may not be obtained though the invention is not identically disclosed as in 102 if differences between claimed invention and prior art are such that claimed invention as a whole would have been obvious to a person having ordinary skill in the art. Rejections under 103 must set forth the basis for combining references and explain pertinence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include contents of 103 rejection (706.02(m) form paragraphs). Provisional rejections combining 102(e) and 103 may be used. Ensure proper factual findings, rationale for combining references, and apply the Graham factual inquiries (scope, differences, level of ordinary skill, objective indicia). See MPEP §706.02 for details and form paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-Precedential/Non-Prior-Art Rejections (35 U.S.C. 101, 112, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rejections not based on prior art include 35 U.S.C. 101 (patentable subject matter / utility), 35 U.S.C. 112 first paragraph (written description, enablement, best mode), 35 U.S.C. 112 second paragraph (definiteness), barred by Atomic Energy Act, new matter, duplicate claims, disclaimer, reissue, res judicata, and other non-art bases for rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow section-specific MPEP guidance: 706.03(a) provides guidelines for utility requirement (101) and interplay with 112; 706.03(c)/(d) cover 112 first and second paragraphs. For new matter and duplicative claims, apply the procedural rules and form paragraphs identified. Ensure the applicant is given constructive guidance for correction when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defects in Form or Omission of a Limitation — Constructive Examiner Action
rubrics_metrics.description: When claims are intended to be directed to patentable subject matter but cannot be allowed because of defects in form or omission of a limitation, the examiner should not stop with a bare objection or rejection but should offer a definite suggestion for correction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be constructive and identify how claims can be amended to be allowable. Where patentable subject matter disclosed but not claimed, note aspects/features unclaimed and indicate that if properly claimed they may receive favorable consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconsideration of Claims After Reply by Applicant (37 CFR 1.112)
rubrics_metrics.description: After reply by applicant to a non-final action, the application will be reconsidered and again examined. Applicant/patent owner will be notified if claims are rejected or objections/requirements made, in the same manner as after the first examination. Applicant may reply with or without amendment unless action indicates finality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.112 provides for continued examination; use it to ensure applicant's arguments and evidence are considered before making a subsequent action. If action indicates it's final (37 CFR 1.113), different response options may apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final Rejection Practice and Withdrawal of Final Rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: Chapter provides rules for final rejection, when proper on first or second action, premature final rejection, and withdrawal of final rejections. Also addresses transitional after-final practice and the procedure to withdraw a premature final rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the specific MPEP subsections (706.07 and subparts) to determine whether a rejection qualifies as final, whether it was premature, and whether withdrawal is appropriate. Ensure applicant's reply periods and rights are respected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation of References — Copying, Order, and Completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules on citation of references in actions: copies of cited references, applicant citation of related art, order of listing, references cited in subsequent actions, and data used in citing references. Also includes effective dates of declassified printed matter and incorrect citation of references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide copies of cited references when appropriate; list references in the order and manner prescribed; note any data used in citing references; correct inaccurate citations. See MPEP §707.05 and subparts for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness and Clarity of Examiner's Action
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner's action must be complete on formal matters, require new oath when necessary, satisfy draftsperson requirements, use correct language in rejecting claims, note all outstanding requirements, answer all material traversed, avoid piecemeal examination, and notify applicants of inaccuracies in amendments. Each claim should be mentioned in each letter, and when claims are allowable that should be stated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow MPEP §707.07 and subparts for detailed procedures including numbering paragraphs, comment on examples, reviewing/initialing, signing by authorized examiner, entry date, and mailing returned Office actions. Ensure the office action is clear and addresses all presentable issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviews — Policy and Recordation (MPEP §713)
rubrics_metrics.description: Interviews between examiner and applicant: general policy on how conducted, interviews prior to first official action, prohibition of 'sounding out' the examiner, requirement that the substance of interviews be made of record, and rules for demonstrations, exhibits, and models. Interviews in special situations and pre-amendment interviews under 37 CFR 1.312 are discussed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substance of interview must be made part of the record (notes, memorandum). Interviews for merely sounding out the examiner are not permitted. Follow restrictions regarding inter partes questions, exposure of other cases, and handling of exhibits. Use MPEP §713 et seq. for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments — Formalities, Responsiveness, Timing, and Entry
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for amendments include signatures to amendments, requirements for fully responsive amendments, handling of amendments not fully responsive, claims presented with no attempt to point out patentable novelty, amendments filed before first office action, claims added in excess of filing fee, amendments after final rejection or allowance, telegraphic amendments, and amendments under 37 CFR 1.312.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments must be properly signed; examiners should immediately inspect amendments sent to wrong group; amendments not in permanent ink, telegraphic amendments, and those containing new matter are addressed. See MPEP §714 and §715 for entry of amendments, lists of amendments entered/denied, and guidance on inadvertent entries and correction procedures. Preliminary amendments should not introduce new matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavits and Declarations Traversing Rejections; Swearing Back (37 CFR 1.131/1.132)
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits or declarations under 37 CFR 1.131 (swearing back of reference) and 1.132 (other traversing affidavits) have different requirements. Who may make the affidavit, formal requirements, factual and documentary evidence needed, and practice relative to showing how much of the claimed invention must be shown, genus-species issues, and predictability questions are covered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between 1.131 (antenuptial or swearing back against a reference with specific statutory situations) vs 1.132 affidavits. Examiners should review affidavits for evidence of prior public use/sale or failure to disclose best mode and for sufficiency. See MPEP §715 and §716 for guidance on diligence, who may make affidavits, and forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence and Weighing of Nonobviousness (Objective Indicia) (MPEP §716)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on generally applicable criteria for nonobviousness: objective evidence categories include unexpected results, commercial success (commensurate in scope with claimed invention), long-felt need and failure of others, skepticism of experts, copying, inoperability of references, and other probative evidence. Evidence must be weighed and compared with closest prior art; burden is on applicant for some assertions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §716.01–716.03 for details: (a) objective evidence of nonobviousness, (b) nexus requirement and evidence of claims, (c) weighing objective evidence, (d) evidence must show unexpected results commensurate in scope, (e) comparison with closest prior art, (f) declared advantages disclosed or inherent. Declarations/affidavits should follow prescribed forms. Commercial success and other indicia must be tied (nexus) to claimed invention and commensurate in scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: File Wrappers and Record Keeping (Arrangement, Papers, Indexing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers in file wrapper must be arranged and indexed: name/residence of inventor, title, prints, data entered on file wrapper, changed classification during examination, index of claims, field of search, foreign filing dates, related applications, public use proceeding testimony, and preliminary handling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow MPEP §719 for organization of the file wrapper. Maintain completeness and clarity of the patent file wrapper. Ensure required data are entered and accessible for subsequent prosecution, appeals, or public inspection where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trade Secret / Proprietary / Protective Order Materials — Submission and Handling (MPEP §724)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures for submitting trade secret, proprietary, or protective order materials: types of materials submitted, method of submission, office treatment and handling, and conditions where materials may be open to the public under certain CFR provisions. Also includes petitions to expunge information or copies of papers in the application file (37 CFR 1.59).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Materials submitted under these provisions must be identified and treated consistent with confidentiality rules. Petitions to expunge (37 CFR 1.59) may be filed if criteria are met (e.g., unintentional submission, irreparable harm, not material under 37 CFR 1.56, fee paid). Examiners should decide petitions only in certain circumstances (e.g., when information was submitted under MPEP §724.02) and may hold decision in abeyance until close of prosecution if appropriate. Use form paragraphs 7.204–7.213 for petition handling.
